stem.text: The height of a weather balloon is H(t) meters, t seconds after it is released. Suppose that \( H'(9) = 11 \). Write this statement in Leibniz notation, and state what it means.

answer_key.label: \( \left. \frac{dH}{dt} \right|_{t=9} = 11 \), so the rate of change of the height of the balloon with respect to time when t = 9 is 11 meters per second.

worked_solution.text: In \( H'(9) \) the function is H, the independent variable is t, and the derivative is evaluated at t = 9, so the statement is about one input only.
In Leibniz notation the same statement is \( \left. \frac{dH}{dt} \right|_{t=9} = 11 \).
It says that the rate of change of the height of the balloon with respect to time when t = 9 is 11 meters per second.

options.label: \( \frac{H(9)}{9} = 11 \), so the height of the balloon divided by time when t = 9 is 11 meters per second.
options.derivation: the Leibniz fraction read as the quotient of the two quantities at the point

options.label: \( \frac{dH}{dt} = 11 \), so the rate of change of the height of the balloon with respect to time, the same at every t, is 11 meters per second.
options.derivation: the point of evaluation dropped, so a value at one input is read as the derivative function

options.label: \( \left. \frac{dH}{dt} \right|_{t=9} = 11 \), so the rate of change of the height of the balloon with respect to time when t = 9 is 11 meters per second.
\( \left. \frac{dt}{dH} \right|_{t=9} = 11 \), so the rate of change of time with respect to the height of the balloon when t = 9 is 11 seconds per meter.
options.derivation: the roles of the two variables exchanged, so the derivative is read with respect to the dependent variable
